en.title: Maximum Non-Crossing Connections
en.description:
The i-th line connects i to match[i]. Two lines cross only when their index order is the reverse of their target order; lines with the same target do not count as crossing. Find the maximum number of pairwise non-crossing lines that can be kept.

This site independently wrote the standard I/O, examples, and judging.
en.input: The first line contains n (1..100000), and the second line contains n match values (1..n).
en.explanation: Example 1: keep the four lines with targets 1, 2, 3, 5. Example 2: all targets are equal, which does not meet the strictly-reversed definition of crossing, so all three lines can be kept. Example 3: the targets are strictly decreasing and every two lines cross, so only 1 is kept.
hints: Find the longest non-decreasing subsequence; use upper_bound to maintain the smallest tail value for each length, allowing equal values to extend it.
